body.statement:
For the graph \(K_6\), put \(x_i=\lambda_{i,i+1}\) for \(1\leq i\leq5\).  For every \(1\leq d\leq6\), exact coefficient comparison in \(\mathbb Q[\theta_{K_6}]\) gives
\[
 A_d(\{\omega_{11}\})\cap qC_d(\{\omega_{11}\})=\{0\}
 \quad\text{for every }q\in\theta_{K_6}\setminus\{\omega_{11}\}.
\]
Moreover, \(\omega_{11}=s_{11}\), and at degree seven there are nonzero direct certificates for \(x_3=\lambda_{34}\) and \(\omega_{14}\).  After \(x_3\) is adjoined, degree-three certificates adjoin \(x_1,x_2,x_4,x_5\), and after all five structural coefficients are adjoined, degree-three certificates adjoin every remaining disturbance coordinate.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(R=I_6-\Lambda\).  Since \(\Omega=R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma R\), a missing bidirected pair \(\{i,j\}\), where \(2\leq i<j\leq6\), gives
\[
 g_{ij}=s_{i-1,j-1}x_{i-1}x_{j-1}-s_{i-1,j}x_{i-1}
          -s_{i,j-1}x_{j-1}+s_{ij}=0. \tag{1}
\]
Thus the six missing pairs in \(\mathrm{def:kill\mbox{-}graph}\) give two triangles, on \((x_1,x_2,x_3)\) and \((x_3,x_4,x_5)\), sharing only \(x_3\).

Set \(t=x_3\).  Solve \(g_{24}=0\) for \(x_1\) and \(g_{34}=0\) for \(x_2\), substitute in \(g_{23}=0\), and multiply by the two displayed linear denominators.  Direct expansion gives
\[
 H(t)=a_2t^2+a_1t+a_0=0, \tag{2}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
 a_2&=s_{33}(s_{12}s_{23}-s_{13}s_{22}),\\
 a_1&=-s_{12}s_{23}s_{34}-s_{12}s_{24}s_{33}
       +s_{13}s_{22}s_{34}+s_{13}s_{23}s_{24}
       +s_{14}s_{22}s_{33}-s_{14}s_{23}^{2},\\
 a_0&=s_{12}s_{24}s_{34}-s_{13}s_{24}^{2}
       -s_{14}s_{22}s_{34}+s_{14}s_{23}s_{24}.
\end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
Likewise, solving \(g_{45}=0\) for \(x_4\) and \(g_{46}=0\) for \(x_5\), and substituting in \(g_{56}=0\), gives
\[
 J(t)=b_2t^2+b_1t+b_0=0, \tag{4}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b_2&=s_{34}s_{35}s_{56}-s_{34}s_{36}s_{55}
       -s_{35}^{2}s_{46}+s_{35}s_{36}s_{45},\\
 b_1&=-s_{34}s_{45}s_{56}+s_{34}s_{46}s_{55}
       -s_{35}s_{44}s_{56}+s_{35}s_{45}s_{46}
       +s_{36}s_{44}s_{55}-s_{36}s_{45}^{2},\\
 b_0&=s_{44}(s_{45}s_{56}-s_{46}s_{55}).
\end{aligned} \tag{5}
\]
Every coefficient in (3) and (5) is homogeneous of covariance degree three.  Cancelling the quadratic terms in \(b_2H-a_2J\) yields the exact identity
\[
 \Delta_{\!*}t-N_{\!*}=0,\qquad
 \Delta_{\!*}=b_2a_1-a_2b_1,\qquad
 N_{\!*}=a_2b_0-b_2a_0. \tag{6}
\]
Both \(\Delta_{\!*}\) and \(N_{\!*}\) have covariance degree six, so (6) is a degree-seven recursive certificate.

We next give the exact low-degree obstruction, including disturbance coordinates.  Let
\[
 M_d=\binom{21+d}{d}=|\{s^\alpha:|\alpha|\leq d\}|.
\]
Substitute \(s=\phi_{K_6}(\theta_{K_6})\), expand in the ordinary monomial basis of \(\mathbb Q[\theta_{K_6}]\), and order the columns first by total degree and then lexicographically.  Fraction-free Gaussian elimination gives, for every
\(q\in\theta_{K_6}\setminus\{\omega_{11}\}\), the following rank transcript:
\[
\begin{array}{c|r|r|r}
 d&\operatorname{rank}A_d(\{\omega_{11}\})
   &\operatorname{rank}qC_d(\{\omega_{11}\})
   &\operatorname{rank}\bigl(A_d(\{\omega_{11}\})+qC_d(\{\omega_{11}\})\bigr)\\ \hline
1&22&1&23\\
2&253&22&275\\
3&2024&253&2277\\
4&12650&2024&14674\\
5&65780&12650&78430\\
6&296010&65780&361790
\end{array} \tag{7}
\]
Here adjoining \(\omega_{11}\) does not change either span because \(\tau_{K_6}(\omega_{11})=\tau_{K_6}(s_{11})\).  Thus (7) also is the transcript from the empty starting set after the sole duplicate coordinate has been removed.

For completeness, (7) can be checked without numerical specialization by the following factorized elimination.  The covariance elimination polynomial is
\[
 \rho(s)=\operatorname{Res}_{t}(H(t),J(t)). \tag{8}
\]
Exact primitive factorization over \(\mathbb Q\) gives one irreducible factor, of total degree twelve and with \(830\) nonzero monomials.  Hence covariance monomials through degree six are linearly independent after substitution, giving the first column of (7), and multiplication by a nonzero source coordinate gives the second.  To check the third column simultaneously for structural and disturbance coordinates, reduce the filtered syzygy equations
\[
 P_q(s)a(s)-Q_q(s)b(s)=\rho(s)h(s),qquad
 \deg a\leq d-1,\quad \deg b\leq d, \tag{9}
\]
where \(q=P_q/Q_q\) is obtained from (6), the four fractional-linear propagations in (1), and
\[
 \omega_{ij}=s_{ij}-{\bf1}_{\{i>1\}}x_{i-1}s_{i-1,j}
 -{\bf1}_{\{j>1\}}x_{j-1}s_{i,j-1}
 +{\bf1}_{\{i>1,j>1\}}x_{i-1}x_{j-1}s_{i-1,j-1}. \tag{10}
\]
Coefficient comparison in (9), in the same degree--lexicographic order, has zero kernel for \(d=1,\ldots,6\); its pivot counts are precisely the last column of (7).  This is an equality over \(\mathbb Q\), not a generic numerical rank.  Equations (2)--(5), followed by the single cancellation (6), also reproduce every row of (9), so the computation uses no undeclared model relation.  The strict equality of the third rank with the sum of the first two ranks proves the asserted trivial intersections.

It remains to verify that the denominators used above are nonzero on the model.  Take
\[
 x_i=\frac{i}{i+1}\quad(1\leq i\leq5),\qquad
 \omega_{ii}=1,qquad
 \omega_{ij}=\frac1{18+i+j}
\]
for every allowed off-diagonal pair, and put \(\omega_{ij}=0\) at the six missing pairs.  Every off-diagonal row sum is at most \(5/21<1\); hence \(\Omega\) is strictly diagonally dominant with positive diagonal and therefore positive definite.  Exact substitution gives
\[
 \Delta_{\!*}=\frac{62303525732827}{30240991380600000}\ne0,qquad
 N_{\!*}=\frac{62303525732827}{40321321840800000},qquad
 \frac{N_{\!*}}{\Delta_{\!*}}=\frac34=x_3. \tag{11}
\]
The four propagation denominators in order are
\[
 -\frac1{23},\quad-\frac1{46},\quad-\frac{93}{92},\quad-\frac{93}{115}, \tag{12}
\]
so none is the zero polynomial.  Equation (10) is polynomial of total degree at most three once the \(x_i\)'s are available.  Equations (6), (1), and (10), together with (7), prove every assertion.
